open_items: ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: fifth occurrence, cycles 150-152 (3 consecutive cycles, 4 hours), resolved by cycle 153, healthy through cycle 187 (no new occurrence, 36 consecutive healthy cycles). Longest occurrence yet (prior max was 2 consecutive cycles, cycles 150-151; before that all resolved within one cycle: cycle 26, cycle 134, cycle 143). Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py). Watch for a sixth occurrence; if it spans 4+ cycles, treat as a genuine regression rather than the known cosmetic pattern.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: ninth episode (cycles 144-145) resolved by cycle 146, clean through cycle 187 (42 consecutive healthy cycles). No fix applied under docs-only scope; standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) carried forward for a session with code-change scope. Watch for a tenth episode, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle or two.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 187: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests, seen on ABS, OECD, ILO, and FBOS. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.

ILO direct-path 403 flap: fourth occurrence at cycle 166 (2026-08-08T00:01:22Z) - 5 of 12 contract assertions broken (references:all, children, descendants, parents, parentsandsiblings), resolved within that cycle, clean through cycle 187 (checked cycles 185-187 individually, all healthy, no broken contract rows). Prior occurrences: cycle 32, cycle 94, cycle 159 (broadest yet at 10 of 12). All four resolved within one cycle. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout every occurrence - only contract-probe traffic drew the 403. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect contract-probe-only degradation. Every run must check intermediate cycles individually since the last run via /api/cycle/{id}, not rely on /api/history or /api/contracts changes (which only diffs the two newest cycles) alone.

IMF references:* 401 flap: first occurrence, cycle 161 (14:01:22Z) - 4 of the references:* contract assertions (all, children, descendants, parentsandsiblings) returned HTTP 401 where 200 was expected, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 187 (no recurrence, checked cycles 185-187 individually). Same shape as the recurring ILO 403 flap (probe volume tripping provider-side throttling, not a general IMF outage). Watch for a second occurrence; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized pattern like ILO's.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 429 flap: second occurrence at cycle 178 (2026-08-09T00:01:22Z) - gateway data, direct data, and direct json all returned HTTP 429; metadata unaffected on both paths. Resolved by the time of that run's live recheck (~40 min later, both direct data and metadata returned 200). First occurrence was cycle 126 (direct data + direct json only), resolved by cycle 127, clean for 51 cycles in between. Clean through cycle 187 (9 consecutive healthy cycles since the second occurrence, checked individually). Watch for a third occurrence; a third episode soon, or broader/gateway-affecting breadth like the second one, would elevate this from a one-off pair to a recognized recurring pattern like ILO's 403 flap.

ECB references:* 504 flap: first occurrence, spanning cycles 182 and 183 (2026-08-09T09:01:22Z and 11:01:22Z approx) - references:descendants, references:none, references:parents broken at 182 (HTTP 504); references:children, references:contentconstraint broken at 183 (HTTP 504); resolved by cycle 184, clean through cycle 187 (checked cycles 185-187 individually, no recurrence). Basic gateway/direct health checks (metadata, data, json) stayed ok throughout - only contract-probe references=* queries timed out. Not the same failure mode as ECB's earlier resolved 406 issue. Same shape as the ILO 403 and IMF 401 flaps (contract-probe volume plausibly tripping provider-side throttling or a proxy timeout, not a general ECB outage). Watch for a second occurrence; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized recurring pattern.
